description:
As-needed medication doesn't always fit a daily schedule. AsNeeded helps you track what you took, when, and how it went. Log a dose, add the details you need, and get on with your day.

MAKE A QUICK NOTE
- Log a dose now, or backdate a missed entry.
- Use your prescribed amount and unit, including fractional doses.
- Hold a medication's Log button to record its default dose; use Undo if needed.
- Add a reason or notes, rate symptoms and effectiveness, and record side effects.
- Find names through NIH RxNorm or enter your own. Add a nickname, colour and icon to help recognise medications in your list.

SEE YOUR HISTORY CLEARLY
- Find doses and notes by medication and date.
- Explore usage charts over 14, 30 or 90 complete days.
- Track remaining quantities and refill dates.
- Export a clinician report to share your records when you choose.

KEEP YOUR INSTRUCTIONS HANDY
Save an optional minimum interval between doses, a rolling 24-hour quantity limit, or both. AsNeeded uses your saved settings and logged doses to show the next saved dose window. Scheduled reminders and optional next-dose alerts help keep these details handy.

These are your saved instructions, not medical clearance. Guidance can't account for unlogged doses or determine whether a medication is safe for you. Follow your prescription and care team's advice.

LOG WHERE IT WORKS FOR YOU
- Log a prescribed dose from a notification after authentication, if saved-guidance checks allow it. You'll get confirmation when it saves. If review is needed, open the app to check the dose.
- Choose whether medication names appear in notifications.
- Open a medication's dose form from widgets, use Siri Shortcuts, or record with the paired Apple Watch app.
- Use larger text, Dark Mode, VoiceOver labels and accessible fonts, including Atkinson Hyperlegible.
- Turn on temporary Demo Mode to hide medication names when showing the app. It resets when the app relaunches.

KEEP YOUR RECORDS YOUR WAY
Medication history and trends stay in local app storage unless you share or back up your records. Paired Watch features transfer information between your devices. Export JSON backups or choose a local or cloud-backed folder for optional automatic backups. Medication recording and history work offline. Search, purchases and some sharing destinations need a connection.

Medication lookup sends search text to NIH RxNorm. Optional support purchases use Apple and RevenueCat, which process anonymous app identifiers, purchase records and technical service information. Medication history is not sent to RevenueCat. See the privacy policy for details.

FREE TRACKING, OPTIONAL SUPPORT
All tracking features are free, with no ads or premium feature tiers. Optional tips and recurring support subscriptions fund development but unlock no features. Apple shows each purchase's price and billing period before you confirm. Manage or cancel recurring support in your Apple subscriptions settings.

AsNeeded is open source under GPL-3.0.

Terms of Use: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/dev/stdeula/

Medical disclaimer: AsNeeded does not provide medical advice, diagnosis or treatment. Follow your prescription and care team's instructions. Do not use reminders or saved-limit guidance as medical clearance, or delay professional care because of information in this app.
promotionalText: Track as-needed doses, check when you last took them and see patterns over time. Set reminders that suit you, with accessible controls and free tracking.
whatsNew:
1.2.0 is here with less fuss and a little more fun:

- Save optional dose intervals and rolling 24-hour quantity limits.
- Log doses with fewer taps, more timing shortcuts, and Undo when you need it.
- Get a clearer look at history, daily trends and refill details.
- Text and layouts are easier to read at larger sizes.
- More dependable notifications, widgets and Apple Watch logging.
- More fixes for backups, imports, recovery and keeping your records intact.

Saved dose guidance uses the limits you enter, so keep following your prescription and care team’s instructions.
